Congo Mining Sector Posts Steady Output Gains in First Quarter

KINSHASA, June 14—The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s metals and mining sector recorded a steady increase in production during the first quarter of 2024, as companies reported higher volumes of copper, cobalt and gold amid stable operating conditions and robust international demand.

According to data released Friday by the Congolese Chamber of Mines, total copper output rose 5% year-on-year to 568,000 metric tons, while cobalt production climbed 4.2% to 37,800 tons. Gold output advanced 3.9% to 12.1 tons, bolstered by improved recovery rates at several major sites.

“The first quarter results reflect the continued efforts of our members to optimize efficiency and maintain reliable supply chains,” said Chamber of Mines President Jean-Pierre Kalume in a statement. “Demand for Congolese minerals remains strong, particularly for copper and cobalt, which are critical for the global energy transition.”

The country is the world’s largest producer of cobalt, a key component in batteries for electric vehicles, and Africa’s top copper producer. The mining sector accounts for over 90% of Congo’s export revenue and is a major employer in the country.

Among leading operators, Manika Minerals reported copper output of 122,000 tons, up 6% from a year earlier, while cobalt production rose 5.4% to 8,100 tons. Kivu Gold Resources noted a 4.1% rise in gold production to 3.3 tons at its flagship site in South Kivu province.

Analysts say the sector’s performance has benefited from stable weather conditions and improvements in road and rail links to export hubs. “Export logistics have been smoother this quarter, helping producers meet delivery schedules,” said Lucien Mbuyi, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Afrique Commodities.

Prices for both copper and cobalt remained firm on international markets during the quarter, further supporting revenues. The government, which receives royalties from mining activities, welcomed the figures. “We are committed to supporting a competitive and sustainable mining industry,” said Mines Minister Marie-Claire Kabemba.

Industry officials expect output growth to continue in the coming months, driven by ongoing investments in infrastructure and processing capacity. No significant operational disruptions were reported during the period.
